evidence.paraphrase: Mudgala tells Dakṣa the campaign’s purpose. Matsara and demons approach Śukra, request consecration as their king and receive his agreement. Named chiefs assemble; Veda-knowing Brahmins consecrate Matsara with Ṛg/Yajus/Sāman formulas, Uśanas directing the rites. The assembly rejoices and returns home.

evidence.paraphrase: Matsara summons the Asuras to conquer the three worlds. Fourfold forces muster with arms, trees, rocks and mountains: infantry, decorated elephants, swift horsemen, chariots and other animal mounts. His decorated chariot has one hundred asses; both sons ride horses ahead, Virocana and other chiefs around him.

evidence.paraphrase: Demon forces defeat terrestrial rulers: some flee, some surrender, warriors die fighting. Sons of dead rulers are installed as tributaries; surrendered kings retain office. Demons govern rulerless regions and are stationed beside local kings. Matsara rejoices after conquering the islanded earth.

evidence.paraphrase: Demons destroy Nāga gardens in Pātāla. Vāsuki, Takṣaka, Kambala and Aśvatara lead resistance: arms and missiles first repel demons; returning chiefs repel Nāgas. Serpent poison-flames burn demons, weapons and mounts; Śukra’s vidyā removes poison. A Garuḍa missile produces bird assailants, burnt by Vāsuki’s poison-fire. Virocana and chiefs themselves become Garuḍas by māyā and overwhelm Nāgas.

evidence.paraphrase: Śeṣa comes conciliating, asks why fellow Pātāla residents wage war, and addresses demons as brothers. Virocana demands submission to Matsara’s universal authority or destruction. Śeṣa agrees, offers annual tribute and jewels, withdraws with Vāsuki and others. Victorious demons march against Varuṇa.

evidence.paraphrase: Matsara sends Varuṇa an ultimatum: submit in office or be killed. Makara-mounted Varuṇa advances with noose and aquatic forces. Virocana, Mahiṣāsura, Śumbha and Andhaka fight them. After three days demons fall; Kāvya restores their awareness, battle resumes and Virocana captures Varuṇa. Kubera hears the news and flees to Śiva on Kailāsa; demons occupy Alakā and march with captive Varuṇa against Yama.

evidence.paraphrase: Demons proceed with captive Yama to Amarāvatī. Agni, Vāyu, Viśvedevas, Sādhyas, Rudras, Vasus, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Vidyādharas, planets, moon, sun and Ādityas join Indra on Airāvata with vajra. Seven nights end in demon flight and fainting chiefs. Sundarapriya attacks the gods; Indra’s vajra does not move him. He disables Airāvata, seizes Indra by the foot and captures him. evidence.paraphrase: Fleeing gods ask Kaśyapa to protect them and release Indra. With Vasiṣṭha, gods and sages, Kaśyapa petitions Brahmā to restore proper stations. Brahmā admits Matsara’s Śiva-boon makes him unconquerable and takes them to Viṣṇu, who also admits inability. Viṣṇu chooses refuge at Kailāsa rather than submission, predicts Matsara will take Vaikuṇṭha and Satyaloka but spare Kailāsa out of devotion. Śiva remains anxious.
